Counterfactual Validation}

To verify that $\Gamma$-based allocation is causal rather than self-fulfilling,
we compare three groups under an equal \emph{rank} budget ($\sum_k \mathrm{rank}_k = C = 64$, following~(A3)) on LLaVA:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Theory} ($r = 4$): The rank predicted to minimize alignment
    degradation by the CLIP structural law ($5$ seeds).
    \item \textbf{Random}: Rank randomly drawn from $\{4,16,32,64\}$
    ($5$ seeds $\times$ $3$ draws $= 15$ runs).
    \item \textbf{Violation}: High rank forced on alignment-sensitive blocks
    ($r = 16$, $r = 32$; $5$ seeds each).
\end{itemize}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.85\linewidth]{figures/fig2_counterfactual.png}
\caption{Counterfactual validation. Theory (r=4) achieves low alignment
degradation with small variance. Random allocation suffers $30\times$ larger
standard deviation ($808$ vs.\ $27$). Violation at r=16 causes severe damage
($\Delta E = +1508$);
violation at r=32 causes complete collapse (all NaN).}
\label{fig:counterfactual}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Result.} (Figure~\ref{fig:counterfactual}) Theory achieves
$\Delta E = -108 \pm 27$ (mean $\pm$ sample std over 5 seeds). Random allocation produces $\Delta E = 491 \pm 808$ (sample std over 15 runs)---the
standard deviation is $30\times$ larger ($808$ vs.\ $27$), demonstrating
that $\Gamma$-based prediction eliminates allocation uncertainty.
Violation at $r = 16$ inflicts severe damage ($+1508 \pm 155$); at
$r = 32$, all 5 seeds collapse (NaN).

different uncertainty profiles. The Theory group's $\Delta E$ distribution

reproducible alignment improvement. The Random group's distribution is
